lines: Bad omens <pulse>linger</pulse> longer than most people think.
I once made a remedy so bitter the patient got better out of spite.
After a hard night, even the brewing stand sounds tired in the morning.
There is a story from the brewing stand, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Most stories here begin with someone saying, 'It will only take a moment.' They are always wrong.
I remember the smell of rain, the sound of the bell, and everyone suddenly pretending they had a plan.
The funny part came later. At the time, nobody was laughing.
A village story changes depending on who got embarrassed in it.
I could make it grand, but honestly, it was mostly mud, noise, and bad timing.
Still, we tell it because we made it through, and that makes people stand a little straighter.
Once a potion turned the wrong color and still worked, which made nobody comfortable.
A child brought me a scraped knee and demanded heroic treatment. I used a clean cloth.
During one storm, half the village came inside just to hear another voice.
I once blessed a doorway after three people tripped there. The floor kept its secrets.
A trader asked for luck and paid in buttons. The buttons were lucky enough, I suppose.
There was a night when the bell rang and every candle stayed lit. We still talk softly about it.
I brewed for a fever through sunrise and learned how long a single hour can be.
Once a golem stood outside the chapel like it wanted advice and refused to ask.
A villager apologized to a bottle after dropping it. Exhaustion makes people formal.
I saw fear leave a room slowly, one cup of water at a time.
Someone once mistook sugar for a rare ingredient. The potion was useless, but morale improved.
I kept vigil through a raid and counted every footstep home.
A lost child found the chapel by following the smell of soup. That counts as guidance.
The oldest candle here has outlasted many arguments and one very bold cat.
I once told a worried farmer to breathe, and the whole room tried it too.
